verdict.reason: may interrupt a resource clients use by name (90%)

state:
An OpenTofu (Terraform) plan is about to be applied to an AWS account (one region). Running applications use these resources by name: they read and write objects, table items, queue messages, secrets and parameters, and invoke functions. Applying the plan carries out the resource changes below in dependency order. Replacing a resource destroys the old one and then creates the new one, unless the plan says the new one is created first (create_before_destroy). If a change fails, the apply stops there; the changes already made stay made.

Current state:
aws_s3_bucket.b: bucket vaws-s14-data; holds 21 objects; versioning never enabled; force_destroy = false in the state
aws_s3_object.o: object config/app.json in bucket vaws-s14-data, written by OpenTofu from the configuration; same content as OpenTofu wrote

Actions, in order:
1. Replace aws_s3_object.o (destroy the old one, then create the new one, forced by the change to key): key: "config/app.json" -> "config/app-v2.json"

How these resources behave: An aws_s3_object whose configured content changes is written again over the object at that key; in a bucket with versioning enabled the content it replaces stays as a noncurrent version, otherwise it is gone.

The questions are about the state after all these actions.
